newsitem.title: USA: Appeals court rules for the Gap in Lauder suit.
newsitem.headline: Appeals court rules for the Gap in Lauder suit.

text.p: A federal appeals court on Tuesday reversed a lower court ruling that stopped The Gap Inc. from using "100 %" in trademarks on personal care products and bathroom furnishings sold at its Old Navy Clothing Co. stores.

The Second Circuit Court of Appeals said that the district court erred in its analysis that found that the Gap's use of of terms such as "100% Body Care" on its products would cause consumers to confuse the items with an Estee Lauder Inc.' trademarked moisturizer.
The appeals court sent the case back to the district court where it is to be dismissed.

The Estee Lauder product, which is packaged in aquamarine glass bottles, contains the lines "100% Time Release Moisturizer with BioMineral Water." The moisturizer, which sells for $32.50 in the 1.7 ounce size, is sold at upscale outlets such as department stores.

Gap's "100% Body Care" products are packaged in plastic bottles and are labeled with such names as "Groovy Grapefruit," "Some Are Pink," and "Positively Purple." They are to be sold at a much lower price at Old Navy stores, which display merchandise on industrial shelving.

The appeals court found that consumers would not be confused by the two products for several reasons including that the packaging is very different and that the items are sold in different kinds of stores.
